Question researched

Do air-source heat pumps work in Nordic winters?

Yes. Cold-climate models keep heating efficiently well below freezing, and they use less than half the electricity of resistance heating over a winter.

  • Cold-climate models still deliver more heat than the electricity they use at minus 20 degrees.→ 01Medium
  • Running costs fall by more than half against resistance heating.→ 02Medium
  • Backup heat is still needed for the coldest days.→ 01Low

01

Cold-climate models keep working well below freezing

Models built for cold climates still deliver about twice the heat of the electricity they use at minus 15 degrees. Below minus 25 degrees most need a backup heater.

Evidence and caveats

Field trials in cold regions measured a seasonal efficiency of 2 to 3 for cold-climate units12. Efficiency falls as the outdoor temperature drops, and most units switch to resistance backup on the coldest days1.

Caveat

The trials cover detached houses only.

Full note

02

Heat pumps cut heating electricity by more than half

Over a full winter a heat pump uses less than half the electricity that resistance heating needs for the same warmth. The saving is smaller in the coldest months.

Evidence and caveats

Measured household data shows a 55 to 65 percent drop in heating electricity after the switch2.
